newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's rates KEB A$180 mln Eurobond A3.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates KEB A$180 mln Eurobond A3.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it had assigned a rating of A3 to Korea Exchange Bank's A$180 million issue of Kangaroo Eurobonds.

The rating reflected the bank's low profitability, heavy policy loan burden and poor asset quality and the expectation of full privatisation of the bank in the near future, Moody's said in a statement.

Korea Exchange Bank's existing debt is rated A3 (senior) and Baa1 (subordinated), and the bank is rated Prime-2 for its short term obligations, including its U.S. and Euro commercial paper programmes.
Financial strength of the bank is rated D, Moody's said.

The rating agency said the Korea Exchange Bank, the largest commercial bank in Korea, suffered from many problems shared by most of the large Korean banks. It had many loans outstanding, which contributed to its very poor asset quality.

Loan quality in Korea was expected to continue to deteriorate at a time when economic problems appeared to be worsening and export companies in particular were facing increasing difficulties, Moody's said.

The bank is 48 percent owned by the Bank of Korea, the country's central bank, but is expected to be sold at some time in the future as it is no longer a vehicle for government borrowing, Moody's said.
